storm.combination_name: Storm 1.0, the graph network and its Allen–Dynes route, averaged
storm.gnn: graph network 2.0 (weight averaging + Allen–Dynes head + crystal descriptors)

check.about: out of fold on the conventional 3DSC materials that Alexandria also has: of those given at least an even chance, the share that superconduct, against the share among the others

rule: only our own finds: nothing that SuperCon, 3DSC, the Alexandria or JARVIS electron-phonon data or our list of others' claims already has, and nothing made of exactly the elements of a known superconductor
caveat: Storm predicts the DFT (Allen-Dynes, μ* = 0.10) Tc of a structure that DFT says is stable or nearly so; a candidate is a prediction until a full electron-phonon calculation and then an experiment check it

check.about: out of fold on the 3DSC entries: of the compounds Hurricane gave at least an even chance, the share that superconduct, against the share among the others

reliability.about: false alarms: the share of held-out background compounds (JARVIS-DFT compounds with no superconductivity record that Radar sends to Hurricane) given at least an even chance of superconducting; an upper bound, as a few of them may superconduct
reliability.cite: T. Konno et al., Phys. Rev. B 103, 014509 (2021)

pool.rule: within 50 meV/atom of the convex hull, a band gap of at most 1 eV, magnetic or not, 2 to 5 elements, up to 40 atoms in the cell, elements Hurricane's training data covers; the list holds the 354 that Radar sends to Hurricane, one per chemical system

hurricane.caveat: Hurricane learned measured Tc from cuprates, iron-based, heavy-fermion compounds and other oxides; it gives the chance that a compound superconducts and its Tc if it does. Many of these compounds would need doping or pressure, and a candidate is a prediction until an experiment checks it
